addresses.name: CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount(int* out@ESI, CCountry* country@stack:4, CTechnologyCategory* category@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which the build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this). Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000: below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 per point; above it 50 per point with everything past 1.000 halved first. Then adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94, and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

**The out pointer travels in ESI, not on the stack** - that is the whole of why the recorded signature wanted ret 12 and the function does ret 8. Only two things are pushed, the country and the category; ESI is never written in the body, only read (every store is `mov [esi], ...`), and the return is `mov eax, esi` at 0x4E1BCA.
addresses.evidence: Read off the body and settled by the call sites, which are independent of anything recorded. Body (disasm.py rva:0xE1AC0, VA 0x4E1AC0): standard ebp frame, `mov ebx, [ebp+8]` at 0x4E1AD2 and every CCountry field comes off ebx (+0x6A8, +0x698, +0xDF8, +0xDA8), so [ebp+8] is the country; `mov eax, [ebp+0xC]` at 0x4E1B2B then `mov edi, [eax+0x5C]` is the category and its index, so [ebp+0xC] is the category. There is no third stack read: the only other ebp displacements in the whole body are the locals [ebp-4] and [ebp-8] carved by `sub esp, 8`. ESI is read at 0x4E1B5D, 0x4E1B63, 0x4E1B69, 0x4E1B6F, 0x4E1BAA, 0x4E1BBE, 0x4E1BC3 and 0x4E1BC7 and never assigned, never pushed and never popped, and 0x4E1BCA returns it - an input register, not a callee-saved one. The function ends `ret 8` at 0x4E1BD0 and cfg.walk finds that as the only ret. All ten direct callers (findRefs.py --callers 0x4E1AC0: 0x41B3BB, 0x463DCA, 0x485B82, 0x4DFDD0, 0x4DFE30, 0x4E1922, 0x4E19E8, 0x51D34F, 0x6C4FC0, 0x7D1A19) have the identical shape - two pushes, then `lea esi, <a local>` in the last instruction or two before the call, and no `add esp` afterwards. Three checked byte by byte: 0x41B3B5 `push eax` (category) / `push esi` (country) / `lea esi, [esp+0x18]` / call; 0x4DFDCB `push eax` / `push ebx` / `lea esi, [ebp+0xC]` / call; 0x7D1A09 `push eax` / `push edi` / `lea esi, [esp+0x38]` / call, and at that site edi is the country independently, because 0x7D19F8 reads `[edi+0xDF8]`, the same CTechnologyStatus pointer the body reads off ebx. Every caller then dereferences the returned pointer (`mov esi, [eax]` / `mov ecx, [eax]`), which is what an out pointer returned in eax looks like. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a caller that pushes three arguments, or that does `add esp, 8`/`add esp, 0xC` after the call, or one that reaches the call with ESI holding something other than a freshly lea'd 4-byte slot - any of those would mean ESI is incidental and the third argument is really on the stack. It would also be wrong if the body were entered anywhere but 0x4E1AC0, but the preceding bytes are int3 padding and 0x4E1AC0 is the target of all ten calls, so it is the function start.
addresses.revises: wave 2: checkSignatures refused the recorded signature - it implied ret 12 against a function that does ret 8. The out pointer is in ESI, not on the stack: ESI is read eight times and never written, and all ten callers push only the country and the category and clean nothing.

addresses.name: CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute(CDistributeReinforcement* this, CFixedPoint* result@stack:4, __int64 available@stack:8, bool flag@stack:16)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 0 of its virtual table, and where the manpower tooltip's two numbers come from.** The class derives from `CDistributionSetting`, so this is the reinforcement slider spending what it has been allocated; every sibling distributor - supply, upgrade, production, research, consumer goods, lend lease, NCO, diplomacy, espionage - has its own body at the same slot.

It zeroes `CCountry +0xA98`, `+0xA9C` and `+0xAA0`, then walks the country's units and every subunit under each, and rebuilds all three from nothing. `this + 0x18` is the country throughout.

**The stack arguments are three, not one**, which is why the recorded signature wanted ret 4 and the function does ret 16: a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8] for the eight-byte fixed point it answers, the amount it has been given as a 64-bit `fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>` split across [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10], and a byte flag at [ebp+0x14]. This body ignores the flag; the consumer-goods (0x118C50) and production (0x119D10) bodies read it and skip their last step when it is set. `__int64` is written for the middle argument only so the arithmetic sizes - it is the same fixed point type as the return.
addresses.evidence: Body: `mov ebx, ecx` at 0x51BA8D with no stack read for it, so `this` is in ecx - __thiscall. cfg.walk over the body finds exactly one ret, `ret 0x10` at 0x51C669, and exactly three argument displacements: [ebp+0xC] (0x51BA88), [ebp+0x10] (0x51BA81) and [ebp+8] (0x51C629); the [ebp+8] reads at 0x51C695 and beyond belong to the next function, past the ret. The pair at +0xC/+0x10 is one 64-bit value and not two ints: 0x51BA87-0x51BA95 pushes [ebp+0x10], [ebp+0xC], [this+0xC], [this+8] and calls 0x799AF0 (__allmul, already named), then `shrd eax, edx, 0xF` / `sar edx, 0xF` - a 64-bit multiply of two fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15> values, and the 15 is the fraction width the constructor at 0x4C9E0D confirms by storing 0x8000 as the initial 1.0. [ebp+8] is the hidden return: 0x51C629 loads it into edi, 0x51C630/0x51C636 zero [edi] and [edi+4] - eight bytes - and 0x51C65A returns edi in eax. 4 + 8 + 4 = 16 = the ret. The two call sites settle it independently, and both are loops over CCountry+0x5F4, the vector of CDistributionSetting* that 0x4C9C64 fills and into which 0x4C9E17 writes CDistributeReinforcement's vftable 0x15C223C. At 0x4DB509-0x4DB537: `mov ecx, [eax+esi*4]` (this), `push 0` (the flag, pushed first so highest), `sub esp, 8` then `mov [edi], eax` / `mov [edi+4], edx` (the 64-bit, from CCountry+0x604 shifted left 15), `mov edx, [ecx]` / `mov edx, [edx]` (slot 0), `lea eax, [ebp-0x24]` / `push eax` (the result, pushed last so lowest), `call edx` - and the next instruction is `mov eax, [ebx+0x5F8]`, no stack cleanup, so the callee's 16 is right. 0x65C1B0-0x65C1DD is the same shape over the same vector with `push 1` and a zero amount, and again nothing is cleaned afterwards. All five sibling slot-0 bodies checked (0x118C50, 0x11AA80, 0x119D10, 0x11CE60, 0x11F620) end in `ret 0x10` and use the same three displacements, two of them also reading the [ebp+0x14] byte (`cmp byte ptr [ebp+0x14], 0` at 0x518DE8 and 0x51A213), which is what makes it a bool rather than a dword. `flag` is deliberately left unnamed: both values occur across the two call sites and the step it guards differs between siblings, so what it means is not settled. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: a third slot-0 call site that pushes a different number of dwords, or that cleans the stack itself, or a sibling body at slot 0 ending in anything but ret 0x10; and if [ebp+0xC]/[ebp+0x10] were ever used apart - one read without the other, or one of them handed to something taking a single dword - the 64-bit reading would be wrong and they would be two separate arguments.
addresses.revises: wave 2: checkSignatures refused the recorded signature - it implied ret 4 against a function that does ret 16. The twelve missing bytes are a 64-bit fixed point pushed as a pair and a byte flag; [ebp+8] is the hidden return pointer.

addresses.name: __allrem
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT signed 64-bit remainder (llrem.asm). With the two saved registers on the stack the dividend is at [esp+0xC..0x13] and the divisor at [esp+0x14..0x1B]; remainder in edx:eax; callee cleans 16 bytes (ret 0x10). **The remainder takes the dividend's sign alone**, which is what tells it apart from __alldiv at 0x799980: the two bodies are otherwise the same shape, but __alldiv has `inc edi` on both the dividend branch (0xB9998D) and the divisor branch (0xB999A9) and negates when exactly one operand was negative, while this one has `inc edi` on the dividend branch (0xB99A3C) and **none** on the divisor branch at 0xB99A56, so the flag counts only the dividend - and the tail tests it with `jns` rather than __alldiv's `jne`. It is signed, not __aullrem, which has no sign handling at all. 7 direct call sites.
addresses.evidence: Instruction-for-instruction against the published MSVC CRT llrem.asm, checked without leaning on the earlier report. Prologue `push ebx / push edi / xor edi,edi` - llrem saves two registers where lldiv saves three, which is why every displacement here is four lower than the corresponding one in __alldiv. The source's DVND equ [esp+12] and DVSR equ [esp+20] reproduce every displacement in the body: 0xB99A34 [esp+0x10] = HIWORD(DVND), 0xB99A3D [esp+0xC] = LOWORD(DVND), 0xB99A50 [esp+0x18] = HIWORD(DVSR), 0xB99A6F [esp+0x14] = LOWORD(DVSR). Then the easy path when the divisor's high word is zero - two chained `div ecx` at 0xB99A79/0xB99A7F followed by `mov eax, edx`, llrem keeping the REMAINDER where lldiv at 0xB999CD keeps the quotient in ebx - the shr/rcr normalisation loop at 0xB99A98, the multiply-back at 0xB99AA8/0xB99AAD, the correction at 0xB99AC3 which subtracts the divisor back out of the product (llrem) rather than decrementing the quotient (lldiv's `dec esi` at 0xB99A15), the final `sub eax,[esp+0xC] / sbb edx,[esp+0x10]` at 0xB99ACB that forms dividend-minus-product, and `dec edi / jns` at 0xB99AD3 against lldiv's `dec edi / jne` at 0xB99A1B - exactly the difference a one-way sign flag makes. It ends `ret 0x10` at 0xB99ADF, the only ret. The divisor branch reads `jge 0xB99A6B / mov edx,[esp+0x14] / neg eax / neg edx / sbb eax,0 / mov [esp+0x18],eax / mov [esp+0x14],edx` with no `inc edi` anywhere in it; that branch is at virtual address 0xB99A56, whose rva is 0x799A56 (the 'rva 0x399A56' the request quotes is neither reading of this address, and image.both() on the instruction prints VA 0xB99A56 / rva 0x799A56). A call site confirms it is a remainder semantically and not a divide: 0xB99681-0xB99687 pushes `0 / 0x64 / [ebp-0x2C] / [ebp-0x30]` and tests the answer with `or eax,edx / jne` - a `year % 100 == 0` test - and the neighbouring calls at 0xB9966F and 0xB996A3 are the other two legs of the leap-year rule, with 0x190 (400) loaded at 0xB99676. No stack cleanup follows any of the three. cfg.walk finds no call instruction in the body, so it is a leaf; vtable.py --holding 0xB99A30 says it is in no class's virtual table. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: an `inc edi` on the divisor branch (that is __alldiv's sign rule and so a divide), a `mov ebx, eax` in place of `mov eax, edx` after the easy-path divs (that keeps the quotient), or a call site using the result as a quotient - the 0x64 and 0x190 constants beside it would make no sense for one.

addresses.name: __allshl
addresses.no_signature: A register convention no C signature can express: the 64-bit value arrives in edx:eax, the shift count in cl, the result leaves in edx:eax, nothing is passed on the stack and every exit is a bare ret. Writing it __stdcall or __fastcall would mean inventing stack parameters to make the arithmetic close.
addresses.comment: MSVC CRT 64-bit left shift (llshl.asm). Value in edx:eax, count in cl, result in edx:eax, nothing on the stack, bare ret. Three cases: count >= 64 answers zero (0xB99B4A), count >= 32 moves eax into edx and shifts it by count&31 with eax zeroed (0xB99B40), otherwise `shld edx, eax, cl` then `shl eax, cl` (0xB99B3A). Sign-agnostic - a left shift is the same body for signed and unsigned, which is why MSVC emits one body for both. 4 direct call sites.
addresses.evidence: Instruction-for-instruction against the published MSVC CRT llshl.asm, which is exactly: cmp cl,64 / jae RETZERO / cmp cl,32 / jae MORE32 / shld edx,eax,cl / shl eax,cl / ret / MORE32: mov edx,eax / xor eax,eax / and cl,31 / shl edx,cl / ret / RETZERO: xor eax,eax / xor edx,edx / ret. The body at VA 0xB99B30 (rva 0x799B30) is that sequence with nothing added or missing: 0xB99B30 cmp cl,0x40; 0xB99B33 jae 0xB99B4A; 0xB99B35 cmp cl,0x20; 0xB99B38 jae 0xB99B40; 0xB99B3A shld edx,eax,cl; 0xB99B3D shl eax,cl; 0xB99B3F ret; 0xB99B40 mov edx,eax; 0xB99B42 xor eax,eax; 0xB99B44 and cl,0x1F; 0xB99B47 shl edx,cl; 0xB99B49 ret; 0xB99B4A xor eax,eax; 0xB99B4C xor edx,edx; 0xB99B4E ret. It is the LEFT shift and not llshr/llushr: those test cl the same way but use `shrd eax,edx,cl` with `sar`/`shr` on edx, and their over-31 case moves edx into eax rather than eax into edx. All three rets are bare, the whole body is 0x1F bytes and the next function starts at 0xB99B4F. A call site confirms the register convention independently: 0xB8E8D4-0xB8E8DE is `mov eax, edi / cdq / mov ecx, ebx / call 0xB99B30 / or [esi+4], edx / or [esi], eax` - the value set up in edx:eax by cdq, the count in ecx, the answer taken back out of edx:eax, and not a single push. vtable.py --holding 0xB99B30 says it is in no class's virtual table. WHAT WOULD SHOW IT WRONG: any push at a call site, a ret with an immediate, or a caller that sets its operand up in a stack slot rather than edx:eax - any of those and the register reading is wrong and an ordinary signature could be written after all. `shrd` in place of `shld` would make it a right shift.

slots_noted: 0x11BA60 is slot 0 of CDistributeReinforcement's table (0x15C223C) and of no other - vtable.py --holding 0x51BA60 returns that one table. It is not recorded under vftable_slots here because project.json's vftable_slots has no "CDistributeReinforcement" block, and mergeFindings.py can only insert slots into a block that already exists; it stops with 'not in the plain shape this can edit' otherwise, which would break the whole wave. The entry is a signature correction to a function project.json already names, so nothing is left reading vf_0. Whoever collects this wave should add "CDistributeReinforcement": {"0": "Distribute"} to vftable_slots by hand. The nine sibling distributors each override the same slot with their own body (CDistributeConsumerGoods 0x118C50, CDistributeSupply 0x11AA80, CDistributeProduction 0x119D10, CDistributeUpgrade 0x11CE60, CDistributeResearch 0x11F620 and the rest), so none of them inherits this one and no slot elsewhere is named by it. The other three entries are in no virtual table at all.
